card.name: Java
card.era: Developed early 20th c.; peak in bal-musette c.1910-1960
card.tagline: Fast, close Parisian bal-musette waltz of the early 20th century.
card.profile: The java is a dance developed in France in the early 20th century, probably evolving from the valse (waltz), mainly performed in bal-musette halls between roughly 1910 and 1960 (Wikipedia). It arose from demand for an easier, faster, more sensual waltz that did not require a large hall - couples dance very close, taking small advancing steps in 3/4 time. Its provocative close hold led some 'respectable' bals-musette to ban it. It is played on the musette accordion; the name's origin is uncertain (one folk etymology links it to the Auvergnat pronunciation of 'Ca va?'). A java features in a cafe scene in Jean Vigo's film 'L'Atalante' (1934).
card.insight: The java is the one wholly original dance to emerge from the bal-musette scene rather than an adaptation of an existing ballroom dance (Wikipedia, Bal-musette).
